title: De Moivre's Theorem and its Applications

resources.description: Historical Background, Theorem Statement, Corollaries 1-4, Finding n-th roots of a complex number, Geometry and Algebraic Properties of Roots of Unity

sections.heading: 2.8.1 Historical Background & Theorem Statement
sections.text: Abraham De Moivre (1667–1754) was among the first mathematicians to use complex numbers in trigonometry. De Moivre's Theorem states: For any complex number cos θ + i sin θ and any integer n, (cos θ + i sin θ)ⁿ = cos nθ + i sin nθ.
sections.formula: (cos θ + i sin θ)ⁿ = cos nθ + i sin nθ

corollaries.formula: (cos θ + i sin θ)ⁿ = cos nθ + i sin nθ
(cos θ + i sin θ)⁻ⁿ = cos nθ - i sin nθ
(cos θ - i sin θ)ⁿ = cos nθ - i sin nθ
(cos θ - i sin θ)⁻ⁿ = cos nθ + i sin nθ

sections.heading: 2.8.3 Roots of Unity and their Properties
sections.text: The n-th roots of unity are solutions to zⁿ = 1. They are given by ω_k = cos(2kπ/n) + i sin(2kπ/n) = e^(i2kπ/n) = ω^k, for k = 0, 1, 2, ..., n - 1, where ω = e^(i2π/n).

properties.detail: The n roots lie on the unit circle |z| = 1 and form the vertices of a regular polygon of n sides centered at the origin.
The roots form a G.P. with common ratio ω = e^(i2π/n): 1, ω, ω², ..., ω^(n-1).

items.label: Example 2.28
items.title: Symmetric Powers of cis(θ)
items.problem: If z = cos θ + i sin θ, show that zⁿ + 1/zⁿ = 2 cos nθ and zⁿ - 1/zⁿ = 2i sin nθ.
steps: zⁿ = cos nθ + i sin nθ.
1/zⁿ = z⁻ⁿ = cos nθ - i sin nθ.
Sum: zⁿ + 1/zⁿ = (cos nθ + i sin nθ) + (cos nθ - i sin nθ) = 2 cos nθ.
Difference: zⁿ - 1/zⁿ = (cos nθ + i sin nθ) - (cos nθ - i sin nθ) = 2i sin nθ. Q.E.D.

items.label: Example 2.29
items.title: Power of a Swapped Phase
steps: Factor out i: sin π/6 + i cos π/6 = i(cos π/6 - i sin π/6).
Raise to power 18: i¹⁸ (cos π/6 - i sin π/6)¹⁸ = (i²)⁹ [cos(18π/6) - i sin(18π/6)] = (-1)⁹ [cos 3π - i sin 3π] = -1 · (-1 - i·0) = 1.

items.label: Example 2.30
items.title: Fractional Power Simplification
items.problem: Simplify [(1 + cos 2θ + i sin 2θ) / (1 + cos 2θ - i sin 2θ)]³⁰.
steps: Let z = cos 2θ + i sin 2θ => 1/z = cos 2θ - i sin 2θ.
Expression = [(1 + z) / (1 + 1/z)]³⁰ = [(1 + z) / ((z + 1)/z)]³⁰ = (z)³⁰ = (cos 2θ + i sin 2θ)³⁰ = cos 60θ + i sin 60θ.

items.problem: Find the fourth roots of unity.

items.label: Example 2.36
items.title: Inscribed Equilateral Triangle Vertices
items.problem: Suppose z₁, z₂, z₃ are the vertices of an equilateral triangle inscribed in the circle |z| = 2. If z₁ = 1 + i√3, find z₂ and z₃.
steps: z₁ = 1 + i√3 = 2(cos π/3 + i sin π/3).
Vertices of equilateral triangle inscribed in a circle are separated by 2π/3 (rotation by ω).
z₂ = z₁ · e^(i2π/3) = 2(cos(π/3 + 2π/3) + i sin(π/3 + 2π/3)) = 2(cos π + i sin π) = -2.

items.label: Question 1
items.problem: If ω ≠ 1 is a cube root of unity, show that (a + bω + cω²)/(b + cω + aω²) + (a + bω + cω²)/(c + aω + bω²) = -1.
steps: Term 1: Multiply numerator by ω: ω(a + bω + cω²) = aω + bω² + cω³ = aω + bω² + c = b + c + aω. Therefore, (a + bω + cω²)/(b + cω + aω²) = ω².
Term 2: Multiply numerator by ω²: (a + bω + cω²)/(c + aω + bω²) = ω.
Sum = ω² + ω. Since 1 + ω + ω² = 0, ω² + ω = -1. Proved.

items.label: Question 3
items.problem: Find the value of (1 + sin π/10 + i cos π/10) / (1 + sin π/10 - i cos π/10)]¹⁰.
steps: Let z = sin π/10 + i cos π/10. Then 1/z = sin π/10 - i cos π/10.
Expression = [(1 + z) / (1 + 1/z)]¹⁰ = z¹⁰ = (sin π/10 + i cos π/10)¹⁰.
= [i(cos π/10 - i sin π/10)]¹⁰ = i¹⁰ [cos π - i sin π] = (-1) · (-1) = 1. (Or -1 depending on sign).

items.label: Question 4
items.problem: If 2 cos α = x + 1/x and 2 cos β = y + 1/y, show that: (i) x/y + y/x = 2 cos(α - β), (ii) xy - 1/(xy) = 2i sin(α + β), (iii) xᵐ/yⁿ - yⁿ/xᵐ = 2i sin(mα - nβ), (iv) xᵐyⁿ + 1/(xᵐyⁿ) = 2 cos(mα + nβ).
steps: x = cos α + i sin α, y = cos β + i sin β.
(i) x/y = cos(α - β) + i sin(α - β) => x/y + y/x = 2 cos(α - β).
(ii) xy = cos(α + β) + i sin(α + β) => xy - 1/(xy) = 2i sin(α + β).
(iii) xᵐ/yⁿ = cos(mα - nβ) + i sin(mα - nβ) => xᵐ/yⁿ - yⁿ/xᵐ = 2i sin(mα - nβ).
(iv) xᵐyⁿ = cos(mα + nβ) + i sin(mα + nβ) => xᵐyⁿ + 1/(xᵐyⁿ) = 2 cos(mα + nβ). Proved.

items.label: Question 6

items.label: Question 7
items.problem: Find the value of Σₖ₌₁⁸ (cos 2kπ/9 + i sin 2kπ/9).
steps: The 9th roots of unity are e^(i2kπ/9) for k = 0, 1, ..., 8.
Sum of all 9 roots: Σₖ₌₀⁸ e^(i2kπ/9) = 0.

items.label: Question 8
items.problem: If ω ≠ 1 is a cube root of unity, show that: (i) (1 - ω + ω²)⁶ + (1 + ω - ω²)⁶ = 128, (ii) (1 + ω)(1 + ω²)(1 + ω⁴)(1 + ω⁸)···(1 + ω^(2¹¹)) = 1.
steps: (i) Since 1 + ω² = -ω, 1 - ω + ω² = -2ω. Since 1 + ω = -ω², 1 + ω - ω² = -2ω².
(ii) Note that 1 + ω = -ω² and 1 + ω² = -ω. Their product is (-ω²)(-ω) = ω³ = 1.
Since ω⁴ = ω and ω⁸ = ω², every pair of factors evaluates to 1. The product of all 12 factors (6 pairs) is 1⁶ = 1. Proved.

items.label: Question 9
items.problem: If z = 2 - 2i, find the rotation of z by θ radians in the counter-clockwise direction about origin when: (i) θ = π/3, (ii) θ = 2π/3, (iii) θ = 3π/2.
steps: Rotation by θ is obtained by multiplying z by e^(iθ): z' = z · e^(iθ).
